extraction.name: OpenBookQA
extraction.description: A new dataset for open book question answering, focusing on elementary level science facts and requiring multi-hop reasoning with partial context.
extraction.creator: Todor Mihaylov, Peter Clark, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal
extraction.publisher: Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Seattle, WA, U.S.A.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The OpenBookQA dataset consists of 5957 multiple-choice questions, each associated with one core fact from a 'book' of 1326 science facts. The questions were created via a multi-stage crowdsourcing and partial expert filtering process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Surveys, Software Collection, Web Scraping, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The crowdsourcing process also asked workers to mark a second fact, k, needed for each question q, in addition to f. These second facts, unfortunately, were often incomplete, over-complete, or only distantly related to q.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The small 'book' F consists of recurring science themes and principles, each of which can be (and here is) instantiated into multiple questions. For F, we use a subset of the WorldTree corpus which Jansen et al. (2018) have analyzed for sufficiency for elementary level science.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The subset we use is taken from the 2287 WorldTree facts that were marked as 'central' by the original authors in at least one explanation. We further filter them down to 1326 that appear general enough to be applicable to multiple situations.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A crowd-worker is shown a random science fact f from the set F. The worker then thinks of a second common fact, k, that may be combined with f to derive a new, valid assertion s. The worker converts s into a question-answer pair and extends this into a 4-way multiple choice question by adding 3 incorrect answer choices.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For each question, 5 new crowdworkers are asked to answer it. If at least 4 out of 5 workers answer correctly, it is deemed answerable and the process continues.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question has exactly four answer choices and one associated fact used in the creation process.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: While simple neural methods are able to achieve an accuracy of about 50%, this is still far from the human performance of 92% on this task.
